title: Frobenius action-site realization and preservation of resolutions
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $T_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $g_T=1_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius $\gamma$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let $R_T$ be the pro-etale ring sheaf of continuous $\Omega$-valued functions locally taking values in a finite subextension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\mathcal B$ consist of pairs $(M,\theta:g_T^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M)$ with intertwining maps [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], and let $U:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ forget $\theta$.

There is a small model $C$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ closed under all integer iterates of $g_T$ in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Postcomposition by $g_T$ and its inverse induce mutually inverse site automorphisms preserving coverings and pullbacks. The induced identification $g_T^{-1}R_T\simeq R_T$ transports continuous functions by the object homeomorphism and preserves their finite coefficient field and the local finite-subextension condition. The twisted action site of [lem-sf-twisted-action-ringed-site] gives an additive equivalence $\mathcal B\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(C\rtimes\mathbf Z,R_{\rtimes})$ identifying $U$ with ringed-topos pullback [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] with invertible structural map. Under this equivalence tensor is diagonal, sheaf Hom is contragredient, and their symmetry and evaluation are the usual underlying module maps. The functor $U$ is exact, conservative, creates small limits and colimits, and has the exact additive left adjoint with underlying object $\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}(g_T^*)^nM$ and shifting action.

Termwise forgetting induces a triangulated conservative functor $D(U):D(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal A)$ on unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with natural identities $H^nD(U)K\simeq U H^nK$. Thus it carries bounded objects whose underlying cohomology admits a finite locally closed stratification with pro-etale locally finite free restrictions [def-sf-proetale-locally-finite-free-module] to bounded objects with the same constructibility property. Every complex in $\mathcal B$ admits a K-flat resolution with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and a functorially chosen K-injective resolution [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Termwise $U$ carries these resolutions to quasi-isomorphisms in $\mathcal A$, preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms, and preserves K-injective complexes. All assertions concern the localization of complexes in $\mathcal B$; no identification with fixed pairs in $D(\mathcal A)$ is asserted.

proof.text: Use the existing full lifted category AsSmall of the bounded pro-etale site. Postcomposition by the scheme isomorphism and its inverse leaves the domains and arrows unchanged. Mapping a presieve and then applying the domain-forgetful functor is the same presieve on schemes, so the generated topology is preserved. Transport continuity through the AsSmall equivalence. Equivalences preserve pullbacks.

source.place: Native Frobenius specialization of the action-site construction; bounded model and postcomposition

proof.text: On the original site, postcomposition is continuous and cocontinuous (its inverse preserves coverings). Restriction therefore commutes with abelian sheafification. Lift the normalized comparison through the monoid-object sheafification adjunction, explicitly comparing composite and successive lax monoidal structures. Reconstruct section rings and restrict through AsSmall.down. The unit equation for sheafification proves that the resulting inverse ring isomorphism fixes each finite-subextension-valued generating function, hence the same coefficient field. Prove the concrete ambientModules equivalence using the two inverse restriction functors and the existing internal-to-sectionwise module equivalence.

source.place: Native Frobenius specialization; coefficient ring identification by precomposition

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-twisted-action-ringed-site] to this small site, its translation and the coefficient ring identification of step 2. Its module equivalence is with the fixed pairs for $\sigma=s^*$ on $\operatorname{Mod}(R_T|_C)$. The restriction equivalence $\Phi:\mathcal A\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_T|_C)$ of step 2 comes with a natural isomorphism $c:\Phi g_T^*\simeq\sigma\Phi$; $(M,\theta)\mapsto(\Phi M,\Phi(\theta)\circ c_M^{-1})$ is then an equivalence of fixed-pair categories [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category] commuting with forgetting (its inverse uses a quasi-inverse of $\Phi$ and the conjugate of $c$), and $\Phi$ preserves sheaf tensor and Hom because it is restriction along a covering-reflecting equivalence of sites. Composing gives $\mathcal B\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(C\rtimes\mathbf Z,R_{\rtimes})$, under which $U$ corresponds to restriction to degree-zero arrows followed by $\Phi^{-1}$. The theorem identifies forgetting with ringed-topos pullback with invertible structural map and supplies all its ordinary tensor, contragredient Hom, symmetry and evaluation comparisons. It also gives exactness, conservativity, creation of small limits and colimits, and the exact additive left adjoint $\operatorname{Ind}$ with underlying $\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}(g_T^*)^nM$ and shifting action. These statements use the ringed site of step 1, not a site requiring $g_T$ to be a $k$-morphism.

By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], exact additive $U$ induces the asserted triangulated functor $D(U)$ computed termwise. The cohomology formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives naturally $H^n(UK)=\ker U(d^n)/\operatorname{im}U(d^{n-1})\simeq U(\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1})=UH^n(K)$, since $U$ preserves kernels and cokernels. The identity holds first on chain maps and then on their localized morphisms. If $D(U)(f)$ is invertible, every $UH^n(f)$ is invertible; conservativity of $U$ implies that every $H^n(f)$ is invertible. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] to deduce that $f$ is invertible. Hence $D(U)$ is conservative.

proof.text: By the natural cohomology identification in step 4, vanishing outside a finite interval remains vanishing outside that interval. A finite locally closed stratification on which the underlying $H^n(K)$ is pro-etale locally finite free is the very same stratification for $H^n(D(U)K)$. Thus the stated bounded constructibility property is preserved, without an assertion about fixed pairs in $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Native bounded constructible restriction, from termwise cohomology

proof.text: Apply the existing independent-coefficient K-flat resolution theorem on the small action site. Transport its resolution morphism through the additive presentation equivalence and use its unit to transfer K-flatness and termwise flatness; exact forgetting preserves the augmentation quasi-isomorphism. For the injective resolution, first use Grothendieck abelianness of the module category and then the existing Grothendieck instance for IsoAlgebra of an additive autoequivalence. Apply the generic functorial K-injective replacement directly to this fixed-pair category. Exact forgetting preserves its augmentation.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Section 07A5 and injectives.tex Tag 079P, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck

proof.text: For the ringed-topos morphism of step 3, $U$ is its module pullback. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-supplied-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] to conclude that $U$ preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms. For K-injectives use instead the exact additive LEFT adjoint $\operatorname{Ind}\dashv U$ supplied by [lem-sf-twisted-action-ringed-site]: [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies with $v=\operatorname{Ind}$ and $u=U$. Concretely, for acyclic $A$, $\operatorname{Ind}A$ is acyclic, and $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(A,UI)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal B)}(\operatorname{Ind}A,I)=0$. Finally the cohomology calculation of step 4 shows that termwise $U$ sends every quasi-isomorphism, in particular both chosen resolution arrows, to a quasi-isomorphism. This proves preservation of resolutions of arbitrary unbounded complexes.
